prompt.context: American Airlines (AA) is developing a recovery plan and has asked your firm to propose a plan to increase the number of passengers per flight.
prompt.question: How would you approach figuring out the bottom line impact of increasing one passenger per aircraft in their domestic flights?

clarifying_info.q: Do we have data on AA's fleet, fares, and costs?
Should we consider international flights as well?
clarifying_info.a: No, focus on domestic flights only.

clarifying_info.q: How many hours per day does AA operate?
clarifying_info.a: Assume the company operates 24 hours a day, 360 days per year.

clarifying_info.q: Are fixed costs relevant for this analysis?
clarifying_info.a: The plane is flying regardless, so fixed costs should not be included in the incremental passenger calculation.

exhibits.title: Aircraft Fleet, Load Factors, Fares, and Variable Costs
exhibits.shows: Three tables: (1) Aircraft models with fleet count, passenger capacity, route type, and fixed cost per 1,000-mile flight; (2) Average load factor, round-trip fare, time in air, and time on land by flight type (domestic vs. international); (3) Variable costs as a percentage of round-trip fare by flight type.

framework: Scope the problem: identify which fleet segments are relevant (domestic only) and confirm fixed vs. variable cost treatment
Calculate number of domestic flights per year: domestic aircraft count x flights per day per aircraft x operating days
Calculate incremental revenue per additional passenger per flight: avg. one-way fare from round-trip fare
Calculate incremental variable cost per additional passenger per flight: variable cost % applied to one-way fare
Calculate incremental profit per passenger per flight: revenue minus variable cost
Scale up: multiply incremental profit per flight by total domestic flights per year
Sense-check the result and identify drivers of uncertainty

questions.prompt: How many domestic flights does AA operate per year?
questions.guidance: Candidate should sum domestic aircraft (737-800 + 757-200 + MD-80), compute flights per aircraft per day using total cycle time (air + ground), then multiply by 360 days. Should recognize international aircraft are irrelevant.

math.setup: Domestic aircraft = 180 + 125 + 195. Cycle time per flight = 2h air + 0.5h ground = 2.5h. Flights per aircraft per day = 24h / 2.5h. Total flights = domestic aircraft x flights per day x 360 days.
steps: Total domestic flights per year: 500 x 10 x 360 = 1,800,000

questions.prompt: What is the incremental profit from one additional passenger per domestic flight?
questions.guidance: Candidate should use the one-way fare (half of round-trip), apply the domestic variable cost percentages (10% + 10% + 5% = 25%) to that one-way fare, and subtract. Fixed costs should be excluded because the flight operates regardless.

math.setup: One-way fare = round-trip fare / 2. Variable cost rate (domestic) = 10% + 10% + 5% = 25%. Variable cost per passenger = 25% x one-way fare. Incremental profit = one-way fare - variable cost.
math.answer: $75 incremental profit per additional passenger per flight

questions.prompt: What is the total annual incremental profit from adding one passenger per domestic flight?
questions.guidance: Multiply incremental profit per passenger per flight by total annual domestic flights.

math.setup: Total incremental profit = incremental profit per passenger x total domestic flights per year.

brainstorming.prompt: Now that we know the impact of adding one passenger per flight, what can we do to achieve this goal? What else can be done to increase AA's profitability?

categories.name: Increase number of passengers per flight
ideas: Change pricing strategy (dynamic pricing, promotional fares for low-demand routes)
Offer better customer service to improve satisfaction and loyalty
Enhance the AAdvantage frequent flyer program to attract repeat customers
Improve seat comfort or onboard amenities to differentiate from competitors
Increase seat inventory through more flexible fare buckets

categories.name: Increase overall profitability
ideas: Negotiate fuel prices — fuel represents approximately 30% of operational cost
Negotiate with labor unions to reduce salaries or benefits for new hires
Focus capacity on the most profitable routes
Discontinue or reduce frequency on unprofitable routes
Optimize aircraft utilization and turnaround times
Reduce distribution costs by shifting bookings to direct channels

recommendation: Adding one passenger per domestic flight generates approximately $135 million in incremental annual profit
This is a meaningful lever — AA should focus on yield management and loyalty programs to close the load factor gap
risks: Fares may need to be discounted to fill additional seats, reducing the per-passenger contribution below $75
Increased load factors raise servicing costs (boarding time, cleaning) beyond the 25% variable cost assumption
Labor relations and union constraints may limit flexibility on cost reductions
next_steps: Analyze which routes have the lowest load factors to prioritize capacity-filling initiatives
Model the trade-off between fare discounting and marginal passenger contribution
Evaluate the AAdvantage program ROI vs. alternative customer acquisition spend
